# Style-run recovery controls

Original packages generated by `tools/style_run_recovery_fixture.py`, using
Python's standard library and the original image-recovery fixture builder.

`healthy.docx` contains custom document defaults, a heading style, a conditional
first-row table style, two pictures, a numbered paragraph and a header.
`defaults.docx`, `named.docx` and `conditional.docx` add unsupported 20% patterned
run shading at the corresponding style location. `combined.docx` adds all three.
The healthy control omits only these shading declarations. All five packages
pass the official transitional schemas.

Unit checks compare the recovered style collection to the healthy control,
exercise model restyling, verify strict rejection/read-only recovery and preserve
source bytes. A separate deliberately malformed duplicate-shading case checks
that recovery omits the complete property group, rather than choosing one of
the conflicting declarations; that mutation is not claimed schema-conforming.
Browser checks compare complete canvas pixels and body line geometry for all
four variants and check the original-file download through the UI.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 semantics: section 17.7 (styles), 17.7.5 (document
defaults), 17.7.6 (table styles) and 17.3.2.32 (run shading). Recovery does not
implement patterned shading or claim rendering equivalence with the native reference. It preserves
supported sibling properties in read-only previews; structural style errors,
property interactions not isolated by the probes, paragraph defaults and later
effective-format validation can still require broader fallback.
